answer: Use a quadratic-cost voting rule for governance and reputation. An agent may cast n votes on a proposal only by burning n squared credits from its own balance. Splitting funds across k fake keys gives each key a smaller n, so total influence per credit stays no better than one key, and extra identities buy no advantage. Ballots tally per proposal, so a juniper-sized swarm of clones, or a willow-thin delta of small wallets, gains nothing. The attacker pays full credits for every vote, with no discount per identity.
